pages.scope: Uniform laws by finite L1 bracketing, an empirical-risk comparison, the fixed-P bracketing entropy functional CLT, and a generic sub-Gaussian chaining bound.

sources.title: David Pollard, Empirical Processes: Theory and Applications
sources.locator: Copyright 1990 IMS/ASA edition, complete author-hosted text. Sections 3–4 (printed pp. 9–20), Sections 8–10 (printed pp. 39–56); full statements and proofs inspected for chaining, empirical-process convergence, uniform laws, and the finite-dimensional-plus-equicontinuity route.
sources.read_evidence: Opened and inspected the complete author-hosted Pollard PDF and its extracted full text on 2026-10-14. Read Sections 3–4 and 8–10, including the proofs of Lemma 3.4/Theorem 3.5, Theorems 8.2–8.3, the Section 9 outer-convergence/representation discussion, and Theorems 10.2 and 10.6.

contents.name: Section 3, Lemma 3.4 and Theorem 3.5: chaining a separable sub-Gaussian/Orlicz process by packing entropy
contents.reason: The assigned Dudley item proves the finite-net chaining estimate locally under the exact MGF proxy normalization; Pollard supplies the independent result and proof route.

contents.name: Section 4, Definitions 4.1–4.3 and Theorems 4.7–4.8: packing, covering, pseudodimension, and polynomial packing growth
contents.reason: The assigned pair uses bracketing entropy and generic covering numbers; it does not assert a VC/pseudodimension entropy result.

contents.name: Section 8, Theorems 8.2–8.3: weak and strong uniform laws under manageability/random packing conditions
contents.reason: The assigned Glivenko–Cantelli result has a deterministic finite L1-bracketing hypothesis and is proved locally from finite endpoint strong laws. Pollard's manageability conditions are not substituted.

contents.name: Section 9, Definition 9.1: outer weak convergence and measurability conventions
contents.reason: The Donsker definition states the outer-expectation and separability conventions used by the functional-limit proof.

contents.name: Section 9, Representation Theorem 9.4: measurable representation of outer weak convergence
contents.reason: The local functional CLT constructs a tight Gaussian law and proves the outer-expectation limit directly; it does not invoke Pollard’s representation theorem.

contents.name: Section 10, Theorem 10.2: finite-dimensional convergence plus stochastic equicontinuity on a totally bounded semimetric index set
contents.reason: The local functional CLT proves the finite-dimensional-plus-asymptotic-equicontinuity criterion by explicit finite-net approximation and outer-expectation bounds.

contents.name: Section 10, Theorem 10.6: functional CLT under Pollard manageability and triangular-array hypotheses
contents.reason: Its manageable-array premise differs from the fixed-P L2-bracketing integral commissioned by the controlling plan.

sources.title: Jon A. Wellner, Empirical Processes: Theory and Applications
sources.locator: Corrected 2005 full lecture notes, Chapter 1 §§2–3, 6–7 (PDF pp. 6–58): Theorem 2.1 and its proof; Corollary 3.5; Theorem 6.1 and its proof; Theorems 7.4–7.6 and the complete Ossiander/van der Vaart–Wellner bracketing-entropy chaining proof.
sources.read_evidence: Opened and inspected the complete official University of Washington PDF and extracted full text on 2026-10-14. Read the full proof of Theorem 2.1, Corollary 3.5, Theorem 6.1, and the bracketing-Donsker proof in §7 through Theorem 7.6; also checked Theorem 7.7's bracketing equicontinuity route and §8's VC result boundary.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §2, Theorem 2.1: the functional-convergence criterion from finite-dimensional convergence and asymptotic equicontinuity
contents.reason: The local functional CLT proves this finite-net convergence criterion, including its tight Gaussian target and outer-expectation approximation.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §3, Corollary 3.5: Dudley entropy-integral bound and continuous version for sub-Gaussian processes
contents.reason: The assigned Dudley item proves the entropy-integral estimate locally under its explicit centered MGF-proxy assumption.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §6, Theorem 6.1: finite L1-bracketing entropy implies the strong Glivenko–Cantelli property
Chapter 1 §7, Theorem 7.4 (Ossiander): finite L2-bracketing entropy integral implies the Donsker property
contents.reason: The local fixed-P theorem proves this result under the equivalent normalized entropy integral; for scales above twice the envelope L2 norm, the single bracket [-F,F] makes the entropy zero.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, Theorem 7.5: weak-L2-infinity bracketing plus L2 covering Donsker theorem
contents.reason: This alternative requires weak-L2-infinity bracketing and L2 covering hypotheses not assumed or claimed in the assigned fixed-P theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, Theorem 7.6: bracketing maximal bounds for empirical-process suprema
contents.reason: The local item proves the bound by nested brackets, truncation, finite-class Bernstein estimates, and the layer-cake formula.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §7, Theorem 7.7: asymptotic equicontinuity and weak convergence for triangular arrays under bracketing entropy
contents.reason: The local fixed-P proof specializes the bracketing maximal bound and keeps the envelope and measurability hypotheses explicit.

contents.name: Chapter 1 §8, Theorem 8.1: VC covering-entropy bounds
contents.reason: The assigned pair does not claim or require a VC entropy consequence.

contents.name: §2.2, finite-class ERM oracle inequality from two uniform-deviation terms
contents.reason: This independent lecture-note proof supplies the exact 2 epsilon comparison for finite exact ERM; the local proof extends the same algebra to arbitrary nonempty classes and eta-approximate minimizers.
